description: Loop 10 — Production readiness deep dive. A full audit of the repository against GitHub Actions run history uncovered the single most important fact about this project: of 56 workflow runs across all 9 previous loops, ZERO have succeeded. The iOS app has never compiled in CI, the Android app has never built, and the Supabase and website deploy workflows have never completed. Every previous loop's 'Ship it' verdict was self-assessed from source reading alone, with no green build behind it. This loop closes the real gap between the current state and production: a malformed XcodeGen target spec that fails project generation, Info.plists with no bundle version keys, a watchOS target that imports an iOS-only framework, an Android Gradle wrapper that is a 531-byte shell stub with no wrapper JAR, a settings.gradle.kts typo that fails Gradle configuration, a release build type with no signing config, a development-only APNs entitlement, a missing export-compliance key, and a deprecated Claude model ID in both Edge Functions. Stories are ordered so that the build comes back first and everything else is verified against real CI output rather than asserted.

userStories.title: Fix malformed XcodeGen target spec that fails project generation
userStories.description: As a developer, I need `xcodegen generate` to succeed so that CI can build the app at all. The Seddly target in project.yml declares an `info:` block with no `path:` key (XcodeGen's Plist type requires `path`), and nests a `configs:` mapping underneath `info:` where XcodeGen expects it under `settings:`. This is the first step of every CI job and is the prime suspect for the 56 consecutive workflow failures.
acceptanceCriteria: The `info:` block is removed from the Seddly target in project.yml
CFBundleURLTypes with the `seddly` URL scheme is declared directly in Seddly/Resources/Info.plist
Per-configuration CODE_SIGN_STYLE moves from `info.configs` to `settings.configs` on the Seddly target
project.yml parses cleanly against the XcodeGen spec (no unknown or misplaced keys)
The `seddly://` deep link scheme is present in the built Info.plist
CI reaches the build step rather than failing at project generation
userStories.notes: Removed the invalid 'info:' block from the Seddly target — XcodeGen's Plist type requires a 'path:' key, so the block failed spec decoding and would take 'xcodegen generate' down with it. CORRECTION after reading the first real CI log: this was never the observed failure, because the job died two steps earlier at the Docker-based secret scan (see US-189). The spec defect is real and would have surfaced the moment the job got that far, but it was not the cause of the 56-run streak. The 'configs:' mapping nested under 'info:' moved to 'settings.configs' where XcodeGen reads per-configuration overrides, restoring Debug=Automatic / Release=Manual code signing on the app target. CFBundleURLTypes with the seddly scheme moved into Seddly/Resources/Info.plist. Also removed the redundant target-level 'entitlements:' blocks from Seddly and SeddlyWatch: both already set CODE_SIGN_ENTITLEMENTS in settings.base, and XcodeGen's 'entitlements' key generates the referenced file, which would have overwritten the checked-in entitlements with an empty plist. Share Extension and Widget already used the settings-only form; all four targets are now consistent.

userStories.title: Add bundle version keys to all four Info.plists
userStories.description: As a release engineer, I need CFBundleShortVersionString and CFBundleVersion in every target's Info.plist. Xcode's Process Info.plist step injects CFBundleIdentifier, CFBundleExecutable, and CFBundleName automatically, but it does NOT inject the version keys unless GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE is on. Today MARKETING_VERSION and CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION are set in project.yml but never reach any built bundle, so release.yml's `CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION=${{ github.run_number }}` build-number bump is a no-op and App Store validation rejects the archive.
acceptanceCriteria: Seddly/Resources/Info.plist declares CFBundleShortVersionString = $(MARKETING_VERSION) and CFBundleVersion = $(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION)
SeddlyShareExtension/Info.plist declares both keys with the same variables
SeddlyWidget/Info.plist declares both keys with the same variables
SeddlyWatch/Info.plist declares both keys with the same variables
All four bundles therefore carry identical versions, satisfying App Store extension-version matching
Passing CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION on the xcodebuild command line changes the built CFBundleVersion
userStories.notes: Added CFBundleShortVersionString = $(MARKETING_VERSION) and CFBundleVersion = $(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION) to all four Info.plists (app, Share Extension, Widget, Watch). Xcode's Process Info.plist step injects CFBundleIdentifier / CFBundleExecutable / CFBundleName automatically but not the version keys — those require GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE, which is off whenever INFOPLIST_FILE names a hand-authored plist. Before this, the MARKETING_VERSION and CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION set in project.yml reached no bundle, so release.yml's 'CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION=${{ github.run_number }}' archive override silently did nothing and App Store validation would reject the archive for missing versions. All four targets resolve the same two variables, so extension versions always match the host app as App Store Connect requires. Verified all four plists parse with plistlib and expose both keys.

userStories.notes: android/gradlew was a hand-written 531-byte shell stub whose own comment read 'In production, use the full gradlew from gradle init' — it exec'd a system gradle if one happened to be installed and otherwise exited 1. userStories.title: Add Android release signing configuration
userStories.description: As a release engineer, I need `bundleRelease` to produce a signed AAB. android/app/build.gradle.kts has no signingConfigs block at all and the release buildType declares no signingConfig, so the AAB is unsigned and Play Console will reject it. The android-ci.yml release job passes ANDROID_KEYSTORE_FILE / PASSWORD / KEY_ALIAS / KEY_PASSWORD as environment variables that nothing in the build reads, and passes the keystore secret as a path rather than decoding it to a file.
acceptanceCriteria: build.gradle.kts declares a `release` signingConfig sourced from environment variables
The release buildType references that signingConfig
The build degrades gracefully to unsigned when the keystore env vars are absent, so local and PR builds still work
android-ci.yml base64-decodes ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 to a keystore file and points the build at that path
No keystore, password, or alias value is committed to the repository
userStories.notes: android/app/build.gradle.kts had no signingConfigs block at all and the release buildType declared no signingConfig, so 'bundleRelease' produced an unsigned AAB that Play Console rejects. Compounding it, android-ci.yml passed ANDROID_KEYSTORE_FILE straight through as KEYSTORE_FILE — but a GitHub secret holds the keystore's contents, not a path — and nothing in the build read any of the four env vars anyway. Added a release signingConfig sourced from KEYSTORE_FILE / KEYSTORE_PASSWORD / KEY_ALIAS / KEY_PASSWORD, created only when KEYSTORE_FILE is set and the file actually exists. When it is absent the config is not created and the release build stays unsigned but still succeeds, so contributors without the keystore can verify a release build compiles; the build logs a lifecycle warning in that case rather than failing silently. On the CI side, a new step base64-decodes ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 into $RUNNER_TEMP (outside the workspace, so it cannot be picked up by the artifact upload) and exports the path via GITHUB_ENV; a verification step greps the AAB's zip index for a META-INF signature block and fails the job if the bundle is unsigned; and an always() step removes the decoded keystore. No keystore, password, or alias value is committed.

userStories.notes: build.gradle.kts set 'baseline = file("lint-baseline.xml")' with abortOnError = true, but the file did not exist. When the baseline is missing, AGP creates it and then fails the build to report that it did — so the very first CI lint invocation failed by design, on every run. An App Store build signed with a development APNs entitlement cannot receive production push notifications, which breaks the Pro+ silent-push sync path that send-silent-push depends on.
acceptanceCriteria: The Release configuration builds with aps-environment = production
Debug builds continue to use the development APNs environment
The split is implemented via per-configuration entitlements files or an xcconfig-driven value, wired in project.yml
ExportOptions.plist and the release workflow remain consistent with the production entitlement
The approach is documented in SETUP.md so the next release engineer does not regress it
userStories.notes: Seddly.entitlements hardcoded 'aps-environment = development'. An App Store build signed with a development APNs entitlement cannot receive production pushes, so the Pro+ silent-push sync driven by the send-silent-push Edge Function would have failed silently in production — the app installs and runs, it just never syncs. Rather than fork the entitlements into two near-identical files that can drift, the value is now $(APS_ENVIRONMENT), resolved from a per-configuration build setting in project.yml (Debug=development, Release=production). Xcode expands build settings in entitlements files during the code-signing step, the same mechanism that resolves $(AppIdentifierPrefix). One file serves both configurations. ExportOptions.plist and release.yml are unaffected because they never referenced the APNs environment. Documented in SETUP.md section 4.6, including why hardcoding a literal back into the file would be a regression.

userStories.notes: Added ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption = false to Seddly/Resources/Info.plist. userStories.title: Make SwiftLint pass in CI
userStories.description: As a developer, I need `swiftlint lint --strict` to be a meaningful gate rather than a guaranteed failure. No .swiftlint.yml exists, so SwiftLint runs its full default rule set and --strict promotes every default warning to an error across 120 Swift files. The invocation also lints only Seddly/Sources/, silently excluding the Share Extension, Widget, Watch, and test targets.
acceptanceCriteria: .swiftlint.yml exists at the repository root with an explicit, justified rule configuration
included: covers Seddly/Sources, SeddlyShareExtension, SeddlyWidget, SeddlyWatch and SeddlyTests
excluded: covers generated and build output paths
Rules that conflict with the project's documented conventions are disabled with a comment explaining why
The ci.yml SwiftLint step lints the configured paths rather than a single hardcoded directory
SwiftLint reports zero violations under --strict on the committed source
userStories.notes: There was no .swiftlint.yml at all, so 'swiftlint lint --strict' ran the full default rule set and promoted every default warning to an error across ~14,700 lines of Swift — a guaranteed CI failure once the build got that far. The invocation also passed an explicit 'Seddly/Sources/' path, which overrides a config's included: list, silently skipping the Share Extension, Widget, Watch, complication, and test targets. Added .swiftlint.yml with thresholds derived from measurements of the actual source rather than a template: line_length warns at 200 and errors at 400 (the longest real line is a 370-char escalation-letter template literal; only 14 lines exceed 200), and file_length warns at 800 and errors at 1200 (LedgerView is 1046 lines, CommitmentDetailView 707 — both already decomposed once in Loop 8 under US-153). Disabled seven rules that measure SwiftUI's declarative verbosity rather than code complexity (type_body_length, function_body_length, closure_body_length, cyclomatic_complexity, nesting, trailing_comma, no_grouping_extension), each with the reason stated inline. Relaxed identifier_name's 3-char minimum, which would fire on idiomatic 'id'/'db'/'ok' and SwiftUI generic parameters. Opted into 16 correctness and clarity rules the defaults omit. Scope now covers all seven target directories, verified to exist. IMPORTANT: I could not verify the 'zero violations under --strict' criterion locally — there is no Swift toolchain in this environment and SwiftLint is not installed, so CI is the first place this is actually exercised. Also changed the CI step to fail if the brew install fails, instead of the previous '|| true' which would have let a missing SwiftLint pass silently.

userStories.title: Pin and harden the Supabase Edge Function lint and type-check steps
userStories.description: As a backend engineer, I need deploy-supabase.yml to type-check the functions it deploys, against a configuration under version control. There is no deno.json, so `deno lint` and `deno check` both ran with unpinned defaults — no strict-mode compiler options, no agreed rule set — and a type error that strict mode would catch could deploy. acceptanceCriteria: supabase/functions/deno.json exists with explicit lint rules and strict compiler options
Both deno lint and deno check run against that config rather than unpinned defaults

userStories.notes: Added supabase/functions/deno.json pinning lint rules (recommended tag) and strict compiler options (strict, noImplicitAny, noUnusedLocals, noUnusedParameters, noFallthroughCasesInSwitch), and pointed both 'deno lint' and 'deno check' at it — previously both ran with unpinned defaults, so a type error strict mode would catch could deploy. Rewrote the type-check step to enable globstar, expand the entrypoints into an array, and assert the count matches a 'find' of the function directories before invoking deno, so a partial or empty match fails loudly rather than passing as success. IMPORTANT CORRECTION to this story's original premise: I had assumed the '**' glob failed to expand and that deno received a literal pattern. That is wrong — with globstar off bash degrades '**' to '*', and 'supabase/functions/*/index.ts' matches all six functions. Verified directly: the old form expands to exactly the same six paths. So the glob was working, by accident, and would only have broken for a nested layout. The real gap in this story was the missing pinned configuration. The historical Deploy Supabase failures (2026-03-26, 03-27, 04-02) remain unexplained — their logs have aged out with 410 Gone, so I cannot attribute them. Could not execute deno locally to confirm a clean check: deno is not installed in this environment.

Runner images rotate which simulator runtimes are preinstalled, and the current macos-15 image reported no iOS runtime at all — the only eligible destination was the 'Any iOS Device' placeholder, with 'iOS 18.4 is not installed'. xcodebuild exited 70 with 'Unable to find a destination matching the provided destination specifier'. acceptanceCriteria: No workflow step hardcodes a simulator device name or OS version

The job fails with a clear message if no simulator can be obtained even after download
The resolved UDIDs are logged so a destination problem is diagnosable from the run output
userStories.notes: ci.yml hardcoded 'name=iPhone 16' and 'name=Apple Watch Series 10 (46mm)'. The macos-15 image reported no iOS simulator runtime at all — the only eligible destination was the 'Any iOS Device' placeholder with 'iOS 18.4 is not installed' — so xcodebuild exited 70 with 'Unable to find a destination matching the provided destination specifier'. Replaced with a 'Resolve simulator destinations' step that parses 'xcrun simctl list devices available -j', sorts by runtime identifier so the newest runtime wins, and exports one UDID per platform to GITHUB_ENV; the three build/test steps then use -destination "id=$IOS_SIM" / "id=$WATCH_SIM". If no runtime is present the step runs 'xcodebuild -downloadPlatform' and re-resolves, and fails with an explicit ::error:: if still empty. Resolved UDIDs are echoed for diagnosability. Verified locally: extracted the exact PICK expression back out of the committed YAML and ran it against sample simctl JSON — it selects the iOS-18-4 device over iOS-18-2, selects the watchOS device, ignores isAvailable:false entries, and returns empty (triggering the download branch) for an empty device set. An earlier draft used a multi-line embedded heredoc that broke the YAML block scalar; caught by parsing the file and rewritten as single-line invocations. FOLLOW-UP after the next CI run: the first version of this fix gated on 'xcrun simctl list devices available', which resolved a UDID successfully — but xcodebuild still rejected it, because simctl reports devices whose platform Xcode has not actually installed. The run showed IOS_SIM resolved to a real UDID and the build still failing with 'Unable to find a destination matching' while the ineligible list said 'iOS 18.4 is not installed'. So the download branch never fired: I was gating on the wrong signal. Rewritten to parse 'xcodebuild -showdestinations' for the scheme and read only the 'Available destinations' section — xcodebuild's own view of what it will accept — falling back to -downloadPlatform and dumping the full destination list on failure. Verified the parser against all three shapes: a populated available section (picks the first simulator), an empty one (returns empty, triggering the download), and the placeholder 'dvtdevice-DVTiPhonePlaceholder' id, which the 36-hex-char pattern correctly never matches. FOLLOW-UP 3 (final shape): two further findings. (a) My own errexit bug — GitHub runs 'shell: bash' as 'bash --noprofile --norc -e -o pipefail', so grep matching nothing inside avail() exited 1, pipefail propagated it, and errexit killed the step in 2s before any diagnostic or the download fallback could run; reproduced locally under identical shell flags and fixed with a trailing '|| true', since 'no match' is an expected outcome there. (b) The diagnostic dump then showed the real constraint: this image has NO concrete simulator devices for Xcode 16.3 — 'Available destinations' lists only 'Any iOS Device' and 'Any iOS Simulator Device' placeholders, and -downloadPlatform did not produce any. So the design changed: compiling needs a matching SDK, not a bootable device, so the build-for-testing and Watch build steps now use 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator' and 'generic/platform=watchOS Simulator' unconditionally — which is exactly what those placeholder destinations represent. Concrete-device resolution is kept only for the test run, which genuinely needs one; when none exists the resolver emits a ::warning:: and leaves IOS_SIM empty, and the test and coverage steps are gated on 'env.IOS_SIM != ""' so they skip visibly rather than silently reporting success. This decouples the compile — the single most valuable signal here, and one this repository has never produced — from which runtimes a runner image happens to ship.

userStories.title: Entitlement-bound identity so every paid tier actually gets AI, and the server knows who paid
userStories.description: As a Pro subscriber to Seddly, I need AI extraction to work the moment I pay, without creating an account, so that the $4.99 tier delivers the feature it is sold on. Today extract-commitments and generate-dispute-summary return 401 without a Supabase JWT (extract-commitments/index.ts:168-183, generate-dispute-summary/index.ts:148-163). The only JWT path is Sign in with Apple, rendered only when currentTier == .proPlus (SettingsView.swift:116-133). When the call fails, extractWithAI swallows it with try? and returns 0 (ScreenshotProcessingService.swift:160-162), and the caller still marks the queue item .completed (ScreenshotProcessingService.swift:104). subscription-webhook updates users by apple_transaction_id (subscription-webhook/index.ts:481), a column nothing in the repo ever writes, and send-silent-push only wakes users with a server row (send-silent-push/index.ts:134), so Pro users without one get no background processing. This story replaces all of that with an anonymous identity bound to the App Store transaction: the client sets an appAccountToken, the server verifies the signed transaction, and every AI function gates on users.subscription_tier.

userStories.title: Counterparty promise page: a signed, read-only record the other party can confirm or reschedule

userStories.title: Sealed evidence: hash at capture, keep the original, embed it in the PDF, verify at seddly.com/verify
userStories.description: As a renter heading into a deposit dispute, I want my Seddly export to include the original screenshots and a code anyone can check, so that my record is worth more than a folder of images. Today the dispute PDF draws text only (DisputeSummaryView.swift:106-162), although every auto commitment carries screenshotAssetID and screenshotDate. Nothing is hashed. Worse, when the user deletes a screenshot from Photos, PhotoCleanupService clears the commitment's reference (PhotoCleanupService.swift:7-30), so the evidence disappears exactly when someone tidies their camera roll. Hash-only sealing keeps 'screenshots never leave the device' intact.
acceptanceCriteria: At ingest, ScreenshotProcessingService stores an evidence copy of the image in the App Group container (file protection complete) and computes SHA-256 over the image bytes, OCR text, PHAsset creationDate and Seddly's recorded date, stored on LocalCommitment as evidenceHash; share-extension items (share- prefixed ids) get the same treatment

Success metric: dispute PDFs exported per month, /verify lookups, and Pro+ conversion among users who open DisputeSummaryView.

userStories.title: Thread reconstruction: stitch many screenshots into one dated promise timeline

userStories.title: Escalation ladder: overdue promises walk a scheduled path from nudge to formal letter

EscalationTemplateService already writes per-category letters, CommitmentSharingService.generateReminderMessage already writes nudges, and StatusUpdateService already marks overdue, but nothing connects them. userStories.title: Case Pack: a one-off consumable purchase for a single dispute

userStories.title: Statutory clocks: attach the legal deadline to a housing promise automatically

userStories.description: As someone whose contractor makes promises on calls, I want to dictate a twenty-second note right after hanging up ('Mike said the part arrives Thursday, $340') and get a structured commitment, so that promises that never reach a screen get tracked too. Seddly's inputs are screenshots, the share sheet, the clipboard (ClipboardMonitorService) and manual entry; CommitmentSource has only auto, manual and shareSheet. Calls, where contractors and landlords make many of their promises, have no capture path.
acceptanceCriteria: A voice-note entry in ManualEntryView and as an App Shortcut transcribes with on-device speech recognition only (requiresOnDeviceRecognition = true); no audio or transcript leaves the device unless the user then sends text to extract-commitments
The transcript runs through RuleFilterService and the LEAP-003 NSDataDetector extraction, and for Pro with consent through extract-commitments; the result opens prefilled for review
CommitmentSource gains voiceNote, and the dispute PDF labels these entries as the user's own note with its recording time, never as the counterparty's words
NSMicrophoneUsageDescription and NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription are added to Info.plist and PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy is updated
Audio is discarded after transcription unless the user keeps it, in which case it stays in the app container
If on-device recognition is unavailable for the locale, the feature says so and offers typing; it never falls back to server recognition
userStories.notes: New story, replacing the draft's LEAP-014 waitlist (S-size site plumbing; its store-link half moved to LEAP-014). Recording calls themselves was considered and left out: two-party consent laws make it a liability, so this is a note to self. Competitive rationale: the cited screenshot competitors capture images only; OurFamilyWizard and TalkingParents (draft's pricing URLs, not re-fetched) capture calls only inside their own platforms. Size: M. Success metric: voice-note commitments per active user, and share of them later marked fulfilled or escalated.

userStories.title: Seddly in Messages: an iMessage extension to log and confirm promises inside the thread
userStories.description: As a Seddly user texting my landlord, I want to drop a promise card into the conversation that the other person can confirm with one tap, so that capture happens at the source rather than after a screenshot. Seddly-PRD-v1.md section 13 already names Messages extensions as a way to diversify input beyond PhotoKit; no target exists in project.yml. Every card is a Seddly impression on the counterparty.
acceptanceCriteria: A new iMessage app extension target is added in project.yml sharing the App Group, with a shared scheme and CI build
The extension creates a promise card (what, who, when, amount) from typed input
The card is an MSMessage carrying a LEAP-002 share link; the recipient sees a rich bubble, and without Seddly installed the link opens the /c/ page with Confirm and Propose new date
Responses update the sender's LocalCommitment through the LEAP-002 response path
Creating a card writes a PrivacyAuditService entry listing the fields sent
Free tier allows cards within maxFreeCommitments
userStories.notes: Critic: dropped 'from the last copied text', which would read the pasteboard from an extension and trigger the iOS paste prompt every time. Competitive rationale (draft's citations, not re-fetched): OurFamilyWizard and TalkingParents capture at the source only inside their own messaging; screenshot apps capture after the fact. Size: L. Success metric: promise cards sent per active user and counterparty confirm rate.

userStories.title: Shared household ledger for co-parents and caregivers via CloudKit sharing
userStories.description: As a co-parent, I want to share one ledger of commitments and agreed schedule changes with my co-parent, so that both of us see the same record without a $110-$300/yr court platform. Pro+ is already familyShareable in Seddly.storekit (proplus.monthly and proplus.yearly), but refreshSubscriptionStatus ignores ownership type and there is no way to share data. A CloudKit-shared zone opens the expansion segment in Seddly-PRD-v1.md section 3.4 without a Seddly server ever holding the data.
acceptanceCriteria: App Store Connect family sharing matches Seddly.storekit, and refreshSubscriptionStatus grants Pro+ for transactions with ownershipType .familyShared, covered by a StoreKit test

The Seddly target gains an iCloud/CloudKit container entitlement, and a new SharedLedgerService uses CKShare on a dedicated zone for commitments marked shared; private commitments never enter it, asserted by a test
CommitmentDetailView has a 'Share with household' toggle and shows who added each entry
Edits from either participant appear as timeline events with author and time
Leaving a share removes the zone from the leaver's device and is recorded in PrivacyAuditService
DisputeSummaryView can export a shared ledger timeline
userStories.notes: Critic: the draft asked to 'enable Family Sharing on Pro+'; Seddly.storekit already has familyShareable: true on both Pro+ products, so the criterion now targets the real gaps (ownership type, CloudKit entitlement). Competitive rationale (draft's citations, not re-fetched): OurFamilyWizard $110-$299.88/yr, TalkingParents $7-$32/mo. Size: L. Success metric: Pro+ subscriptions with a shared ledger, and family-shared entitlements in App Store Connect.

userStories.title: Outbound webhooks for Pro+ and Business so other tools hear about overdue and kept promises
userStories.description: As a freelancer who lives in Notion or Todoist, I want Seddly to push new, overdue and kept promises to my tools, so that Seddly becomes the accountability layer under the tools I already use. APIAccessView advertises Zapier webhooks, Notion and Airtable (APIAccessView.swift:105-109), but api-commitments is request-response only: it already supports GET, POST, PATCH and DELETE (api-commitments/index.ts:161-168) and pushes nothing. Server-side state exists only for Pro+ users whose data SyncService uploads, so events derive from sync.
acceptanceCriteria: A migration adds webhooks (user_id, url, secret hash, events[], active) and webhook_deliveries with retry state, under RLS

An Edge Function delivers HMAC-signed events for commitment.created, commitment.overdue, commitment.fulfilled and share.responded, triggered from synced commitment changes, with exponential retry and a dead-letter state
APIAccessView lets Pro+/Business users add, test and revoke webhook URLs, shows recent delivery status, and states that only synced commitments emit events
APIAccessView's Zapier, Notion and Airtable lines describe what actually exists, with the existing PATCH endpoint documented as the path for marking a promise kept from outside
Each delivery is recorded in privacy_audit_log with the fields sent
Function tests cover signature verification, retry backoff, and that a revoked webhook receives nothing
userStories.notes: Critic: the draft required api-commitments to 'accept PATCH'; it already does (index.ts:166), so that criterion was replaced. The EventKit back-link criterion was dropped: CalendarService writes calendar events, and a completed calendar event has no completion callback to listen to. Competitive rationale (draft's citations, not re-fetched): Bump and Clutch export to Reminders, Things, Notion and Todoist; none of those listings mentions overdue or kept events. Size: M. Success metric: Pro+/Business users with an active webhook, and their 90-day retention versus users without one.

userStories.title: Seddly for Mac: capture desktop screenshots and email promises
userStories.description: As a freelancer who works on a laptop, I want Seddly on the Mac to watch my screenshots folder and accept shared email text, syncing to my iPhone ledger, so that client promises made in Slack, email and web portals are captured where they happen. project.yml declares iOS and watchOS deployment targets only. Seddly's freelancer segment lives on the desktop, and the draft's research cites CaptainShot shipping on Mac.
acceptanceCriteria: project.yml adds a macOS destination for the Seddly target (SwiftUI multiplatform) with platform conditions around PhotoKit-only services (ScreenshotService, PhotoCleanupService, BackgroundTaskService), and CI builds it
A FolderWatchService monitors a user-chosen screenshots folder with security-scoped bookmarks and runs Vision OCR plus the existing pipeline
A macOS Share Extension accepts text and images from Mail and browsers
Commitments sync to iOS via the Pro+ SyncService or the LEAP-018 CloudKit zone
A menu bar extra shows the next deadline and overdue count
Free tier limits match iOS, enforced by the same AppConstants
userStories.notes: Competitive rationale (draft's citations, not re-fetched): CaptainShot runs on iPhone, iPad and Mac; Bump is phone-only. Lowest priority because it depends on LEAP-001 identity and a sync path, and the desktop segment is best reached after LEAP-013 gives freelancers a tier. Size: L. Success metric: Mac installs and share of paid users active on two devices.
